Level 2 · Intermediate · Week 3

Lists: Collections of Things

A list keeps many values in order, and the first one is number 0.

What you will learn

  • How to keep many values in one list.
  • How to find an item by its index, starting from 0.
  • How to add items with append and count them with len.
  • How to visit every item with a for loop.
  • How to pick colors that work for everyone.

The big idea: a row of lockers

A list is like a row of lockers. Each locker has a number painted on it, called its index. The first locker is number 0.

Making and using a list

backpack = ["torch", "rope", "map"]
backpack.append("apple")    # adds to the END of the list
print(len(backpack))        # 4   how many items
print(backpack[0])          # torch   the first item
print(backpack[-1])         # apple   -1 means the last item

With 4 items, the index numbers are 0, 1, 2 and 3. Asking for backpack[4] crashes with IndexError: list index out of range. This is called an off-by-one bug.

Two ways to loop over a list

Visit every item Visit every index number
for item in backpack: for i in range(len(backpack)):
    print(item)     print(i, backpack[i])
Use it when you only need the items. Use it when you also need the position number.

Colors for everyone

Some people see colors differently, often red and green. These eight Okabe-Ito colors stay different for almost everyone. Use them, and always add a label, number or shape too, so color is never the only clue.

orange #E69F00 blue #0072B2
sky blue #56B4E9 vermillion #D55E00
bluish green #009E73 reddish purple #CC79A7
yellow #F0E442 black #000000

New words

list
Many values kept in order inside square brackets, like ["torch", "rope"] .
item
One value inside a list.
index
The position number of an item. The first item has index 0.
append
Add an item to the end of a list: backpack.append("map") .
len
Counts the items in a list: len(backpack) .
IndexError
The error you get when you ask for an index that does not exist.
off-by-one
A bug where a number is one too big or one too small, like using len as the last index.
accessible
Designed so that everyone can use it, including people who see colors differently.

CreativeDesign a palette

Choose 4 colors from the Okabe-Ito list for a game or poster you would like to make. Write the list as Python, then sketch your design. Add a label or shape to every colored part, so someone who sees colors differently can still understand it.
